gap_evidence.method: window per micro-batch from CPU rf markers (forward_m{i}/backward_m{i}); device events crossing a boundary are CLIPPED into it; union of clipped intervals; gaps = uncovered time inside the window. Host reconciliation uses the trace's own cpu_op / cuda_runtime / sync events and ac2g correlation ids. No PCM.
gap_evidence.finding: per micro-batch forward window: idle 28-38 ms, largest single gap 3-5 ms; every top gap STARTS when the previous kernel ends and ENDS when 'Memcpy HtoD (Pageable->Device)' starts; no cpu_op runs at gap start -> host-side tokenize (prepare_embedding_inputs, 5 groups/micro-batch) blocks the device
gap_evidence.h2d_is_not_the_cost: microbench: pageable .to(cuda) 0.029 ms vs pinned non_blocking 0.021 ms for one micro-batch of input_ids -> the H2D copy itself is NOT the 3-5 ms; the host tokenize before it is

hypothesis: overlapping the tokenize of group i+1 with the device compute of group i removes most of the per-micro-batch gap

experiment.single_factor: WHEN tokenize happens (inline = current; overlap = tokenize next group while current computes); same snapshot/inputs/tokenizer/H2D/math; F.normalize tail identical to the real embedding_batch

verdict: HYPOTHESIS REJECTED: overlap vs inline flips sign across 6 paired steps (median 0.3 ms, 3/6 negative) -> whole-step FLAT. The per-micro-batch host-tokenize gap cannot be recovered by simple overlap (the host is already saturated by tokenize, so overlapping adds sync points instead of hiding them).
note_on_first_attempt: the FIRST run of this experiment omitted F.normalize (loss ~1568 instead of ~2.9) and its numbers were DISCARDED; the corrected run reproduces the real loss magnitude and is the one reported here.
